title: The Last Thorn
premise: Rafael Okonkwo, a cartographer bound to the Guild of Impossible Things, inherits a dying stranger's map of the Thornlands — a realm erased from every ledger after an ancient war. The map is alive, and it remembers a truth the Guild has spent centuries burying: the war never ended, it was merely priced out of existence by a treaty written in blood-debt. Hunted by Guild enforcers who must silence him and courted by Thornland exiles who would weaponize him, Rafael discovers his own family helped draw the original treaty line — through living land. In the end, Rafael chooses truth over loyalty to the Guild, redrawing the map to give the Thornlands back their borders at the cost of his place in the world he knew, and walks into the unmapped country with the woman he was ordered to betray.
about_author: Dominic Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people caught between institutions and their consciences, and they still cannot resist buying atlases at estate sales.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. We meet the Guild of Impossible Things through its ledgers: bottled storms, borrowed years, one honest lie. Rafael, meticulous and quietly lonely, notices an entry that shouldn't exist — a map, catalogued twice, both copies marked destroyed. The beat is unease: the first crack in a life built on careful records.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Inkwell Door
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into the guildhouse's map room, pressing a folded chart into Rafael's hands and whispering 'the line is drawn through us' before dying. The Guild arrives within minutes — too quickly, as if summoned. The beat is fear and complicity: Rafael hides the map in a moment he can't explain even to himself.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with the map itself speaking in marginalia. Studying the chart in secret, Rafael realizes it depicts the Thornlands — a realm struck from every atlas — and that the ink shifts, recording events as they happen beyond the treaty line. The beat is wonder curdling into dread: the map is not a record; it is a witness.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde Vane, a Guild enforcer raised on her father's cartographic legends, is assigned to find the missing map and the clerk who took it. She knows Rafael by reputation and once, briefly, by heart. The beat is divided loyalty: she wants to bring him in alive, and hates how much she wants that.

chapters.title: Running the Old Roads
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Fleeing the city along roads that predate the Guild, Rafael is ambushed by Thornland exiles led by Brannoc, a scarred veteran who recognizes the map — and recognizes Rafael's surname from the treaty rolls. The beat is vertigo: the enemy may be the only people telling him the truth.

chapters.title: The Treaty of Blood-Debt
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV, framed around a fireside telling. The exiles reveal the treaty: to end the ancient war, the Guild drew a border through living land and paid for peace with the Thornlanders' names, memories, and country. Rafael's grandfather held the pen. The beat is grief and fury — inheritance as indictment.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde corners Rafael but hesitates long enough for the exiles to turn the tables; captured alongside him, she reads the map's shifting margins and sees her father's signature on the treaty. The beat is betrayal turned inward: the institution she served has been lying in her own hand all along.

chapters.title: The Guild Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Guild's Master of Ledgers offers Rafael absolution — restore his name, erase the Thornlands' claim, keep Isolde safe — if he surrenders the map. Isolde urges him to take the deal; Brannoc urges war. The beat is the book's thematic crux: loyalty, truth, and love pulling in three directions at once.

chapters.title: Redrawing the Line
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the treaty stone where the old border was drawn, the Guild's enforcers converge on the exiles. Rafael does the unthinkable: he takes up a cartographer's pen on living ground and redraws the border to restore the Thornlands, anchoring it with the blood-debt clause reversed — his own name entered in the ledger. The beat is sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV, closing. The Guild retreats rather than fight a border that now officially exists; Brannoc's people begin the slow work of return. Isolde, stripped of rank, finds Rafael at the edge of the new map. The beat is quiet resolution: they walk together into territory no ledger records, belonging at last to something unwritten.
